narrative.overview:
Every proposal sells the same person and the same booking flow, each in its own room. The shared floor is product, not style: who Gala is, what she treats, studio or home as a first-class choice, prices in plain view, and a booking that is never more than one tap away. Everything visual sits inside one proposal.

The six rooms, as built:

- **P1 Pastel** (`propuesta-1/`): an airy light page in a single light-weight geometric sans (Urbanist 300). It has a soft bento of rounded tiles, three switchable three-colour pastel combos, and a 4-step booking card set on a pastel gradient.
- **P2 Atelier** (`propuesta-2/`): a deep petrol night page with ivory text and champagne actions. It uses a Gloock serif display over Hanken Grotesk, an interactive body map in the hero, a postcode checker, booking that composes a WhatsApp message, and a fixed tab bar on mobile.
- **P3 Joyero** (`propuesta-3/`): pearl and plum jewellery-case cases. It sets Italiana display over Figtree and uses arch-topped "pieces" in a horizontal vitrine, a sliding studio/home switch that rewrites the page, and a concierge chat for booking.
- **P4 Baldosa** (`propuesta-4/`): the floor of an Eixample flat. Encaustic tiles in three pigments sit on lime-white grout, the layout is counted in whole tiles, corners are square, and only the controls are pills. Bricolage Grotesque runs condensed over Figtree.
- **P5 Stories** (`propuesta-5/`): the site as tap-through vertical story frames inside a phone-proportion viewer. It has highlight rings as navigation, a reply bar on every frame that becomes the WhatsApp message, and Hanken Grotesk 800 throughout.
- **P6 Prospecto** (`propuesta-6/`): the landing page as a printed skincare box and its leaflet. One powder pink is the ground, the ink is deep plum, Gilda Display is set flat, the box has dashed creases and a perforated seal that holds the booking, and the leaflet carries ruled INCI-style lists.
keyCharacteristics: Six self-contained worlds, each in one HTML file with its tokens declared in `:root`.
Every world pairs a pastel or soft ground with one deep ink, and that ink carries the primary action.
Every world uses pill buttons (999px) with a minimum height of 44 to 52px.
Booking is a demo in all six, and placeholder data is labelled in the page.

rules.name: The Proposal Prefix Rule
rules.body: A token belongs to one world. A P4 pigment never appears in P6, and the shared floor owns no colour except the error red.

rules.name: The Live Combo Rule
rules.body: Pastel fills reference the switchable variables (`--c1..c3`, `--t1..t3`), never literal hexes, so the palette chooser repaints the whole page, including the SVG tile fills.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: The ground is one pink at full strength. Depth comes from its deeper step and from paper, never from a second hue.

rules.name: The Champagne Is Action Rule
rules.body: On petrol, champagne means "you can press this". It is not decoration.

rules.name: The Light Display Rule
rules.body: Display stays at weight 300/400. Hierarchy comes from size and negative tracking, never from bold.

rules.name: The Condensed Stretch Rule
rules.body: Every Bricolage heading sets `font-stretch` between 75% and 85%. The display face is never set at its default width.

rules.name: The Caption Highlight Rule
rules.body: The right-column claim sits on white highlight boxes (`box-decoration-break: clone`, 0.18em radius), which is the story text mode. It appears only in that column.

rules.name: The Flat Floor Rule
rules.body: Tiles never cast shadows. A tile is a coloured plane laid in grout.

rules.name: The Sticker Lift Rule
rules.body: Only objects that sit on top of a story (the viewer, stickers, the fact card) get a shadow, and it is always the same short, negative-spread ink shadow.

dos: **Do** take every value from the chosen proposal's own `p*-` tokens and nothing from a sibling.
**Do** keep booking one tap away: a header pill, the hero slots (P1, P4, P5, P6), a mobile dock or tab bar (P2, P6), and the reply bar (P5).
**Do** keep studio and home as two equal options in every booking control.
**Do** label every placeholder value "dato de ejemplo" and every photo slot "pendiente".
**Do** in P4 size and space in tile fractions of `--tile`, with 2px grout between tiles.
**Do** in P4 mark an available option with a dashed 1.5px ink border and the chosen one with a solid border.
**Do** in P6 draw folds only as 1px dashed creases at 40% plum.
**Do** in P6 number list rows only when they are a real sequence (the three phases of a session).
**Do** in P5 keep auto-advance pausable, pause it on interaction, and keep each frame addressable by hash.
donts: **Don't** mix fonts or pigments between proposals, and don't add a second hue to P6's ground.
**Don't** add shadows to P4 tiles or P2 surfaces. Shadows exist only where listed in Elevation & Depth.
**Don't** round P4's tiles, fields or panels. Only pill controls are round there.
**Don't** use the looks the client rejected: 2005-era magazine (oxblood, gold and Bodoni) and holographic night glam.
**Don't** add testimonials, review stars, patient counts or press logos. None exist.
**Don't** add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, glyph icons, or gradient-filled text. See the not-canonized note below.
notCanonized: P1: hero eyebrow pill (.where-line) with a "✦" text glyph — kicker plus glyph icon.
P3: unused gradient-text utility (.rg) — dead CSS.
